statement.p: Calculate the directional derivative of f(x,y)=x^{2}y^{2} in the direction u of \mathbf{v}=2 \mathbf{i}+3\mathbf{j} at the point P=(1,-2). Remember to normalize the direction vector.

static.solution:
\mathbf{v} to obtain a unit vector \mathbf{u} in the direction of \mathbf{v}: \mathbf{u}= rac{\mathbf{v}}{||\mathbf{v}||}= rac{1}{\sqrt{13}}(2\mathbf{i} +3 \mathbf{j}) We compute the gradient of f(x,y)=x^{2}y^{2} at the point P: 
abla f=\left\lt  rac{\partial{f}}{\partial{x}},  rac{\partial{f}}{\partial{y}} ight>=\left\lt 2xy^{2},2x^{2}yight>\quad \Rightarrow \quad 
abla f(1,-2)=\left\lt 8, -4ight> The directional derivative in the direction \mathbf{v} is thus D_uf(1,-2)=
abla f(1,-2) \cdot \mathbf{u}=\left\lt 8, -4 ight> \cdot  rac{1}{\sqrt{13}} \left\lt 2, 3ight>= rac{4}{\sqrt{13}}\approx 1.1094
